mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (and any registered name-change certificate) of the ultimate parent or investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry or the equivalent competent company registry in the investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille track: (1) notarization by a local notary; (2) issuance of an Apostille certificate by the designated Competent Authority of the issuing state, including the High Court of Hong Kong SAR where applicable; (3) no further consular legalization. Consular Legalization track for non-Apostille member states: (1) local notarization; (2) authentication by the issuing state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs; (3) consular legalization by the consular post of the destination jurisdiction; the Apostille track is never combined with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Registration Status of the investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Companies or Market Entity Registration Authority (Hong Kong Companies Registry; PRC SAMR Market Entity Registration Information System for mainland entities)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille track: (1) notarization of the certificate by a local notary; (2) Apostille certification by the state's Competent Authority (Hong Kong SAR: High Court Registry); (3) no consular legalization. Consular Legalization track for non-member states: (1) notarization; (2) Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication; (3) legalization by the destination consulate/embassy; these paths are mutually exclusive and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing formation of the Foreign-Invested Partnership and the UBO information filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or corporate secretary of the investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille track: (1) notarization by a local notary acceptable in the issuing jurisdiction; (2) apostilisation by the designated Competent Authority; (3) no further legalization. Consular Legalization track: (1) local notarization; (2) foreign-affairs authentication; (3) consular legalization at the destination state's mission; no apostille is applied in the consular track.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Limited Partnership Agreement (constitutional document) of the investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing corporate or partnership registry, or a notarially extracted constitutional document certified by the investing entity's registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille track: (1) notarization; (2) Apostille from the issuing state's Competent Authority; (3) certified translation and no consular legalization. Consular Legalization track: (1) notarization; (2) Ministry of Foreign Affairs certification; (3) legalization by the receiving state's consular officer; the two routes are parallel and must not be applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming entity existence, account conduct, and signatory authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank or deposit-taking financial institution of the investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille track: (1) notarization of the bank officer's signature and authority; (2) Apostille certificate from the competent authority; (3) no consular legalization. Consular Legalization track: (1) notarization; (2) foreign-affairs authentication; (3) consular legalization at the destination jurisdiction's embassy or consulate; no sequential combination of Apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, general partners, limited partners, directors, and authorized signatories are screened before admission against (i) the OFAC SDN List and consolidated sanctions lists; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List and UN Sanctions Committee designations; (iii) the Hong Kong SAR List of Terrorists and Specified Entities under the United Nations (Anti-Terrorism Measures) Ordinance (Cap. 575) and the UN Sanctions Ordinance; (iv) the People's Bank of China beneficial-owner information system and domestic Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) database; and (v) adverse-media and consumer due diligence databases. Senior foreign political figures, their immediate family members, and known close associates are subject to enhanced due diligence with independent source verification and senior management approval. Screening is refreshed at least every 90 days and must be repeated before any SWIFT/ACH payment event. This profile is calibrated to the Low_Risk_Standard for a programmatic advertising DSP/SSP platform.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) and the SAMR Online Enterprise Name Reservation and Registration Service; for the Hong Kong layer, the Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Registry / Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Administrative Provisions on Enterprise Name Registration, the registered name must be stated in standardized simplified Chinese characters and must follow the four-tier naming convention in official order: (1) administrative division; (2) distinctive trade name; (3) industry or operational characteristics; and (4) organizational form. A foreign investor name may be phonetically transliterated into Chinese characters, but the transliterated name must be pronounceable, distinctive, not misleading, and must avoid identical or confusingly similar matches in the same industry. Arabic numerals and Latin letters may only be used in permitted supplementary positions consistent with SAMR interpretive guidance. For the Hong Kong SAR layer, an English name and a Chinese name may differ, subject to the Companies Registry's distinctiveness and confusion tests.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written rejection, the applicant may, within 60 days of receipt, file an administrative reconsideration application with the immediately superior market regulatory authority under the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC, demanding a fresh review of the four-tier name structure, distinctiveness, and the commercial necessity of any sensitive token. The appeal must attach the original rejection notice, a revised name chart, and evidence of prior registration or trademark rights. If reconsideration fails or is not decided in time, the applicant may institute administrative litigation in the competent people's court within six months. For a Hong Kong entity layer, a request for review of a reserved name may be addressed to the Hong Kong Companies Registry within 20 days of rejection, supported by legal argument on non-confusion and public interest.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a PRC Foreign-Invested Partnership, a contractual virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding address is not permissible as the registered address. SAMR registration and municipal State Taxation Administration practice require a substantive leased or owned office/service address within the registered administrative division, evidenced by lease contract, property right certificate or licensed sublease, recent utility bills, and on-site signage; banks likewise require such substance before opening a corporate account. For the Hong Kong SAR layer, a registered office and a company secretary are mandatory, and a licensed service provider's shared registered address may satisfy registry correspondence requirements for a low-risk investment holding vehicle, but it will generally not substantiate an offshore-tax-claim or commercial-substance defence and is likely to be rejected by banks unless a separately documented Hong Kong place of business exists.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) executed lease and landlord identity/property title records; (2) utility invoices matching the registered address; (3) employee roster and social insurance records; (4) board or partner meeting minutes; (5) service agreements, ad-exchange contracts, and SSP reconciliation logs; (6) accounting books, bank statements, and tax filing receipts; and (7) registered signage. Quantified risk: for a low-asset programmatic advertising DSP/SSP platform, unannounced physical inspection by the municipal SAMR or tax bureau is estimated at 30-35 percent within the first 24 months of formation and approximately 15-20 percent per tax year thereafter; failure to maintain a substantive address exposes the FIP to deregistration, denial of pass-through eligibility, and adverse banking action.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) of the Laws of Hong Kong, particularly Part 3 (Incorporation of Companies) and Part 11 (Accounts and Audit); Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 38) for general partnership law; Limited Partnerships Fund Ordinance (Cap. 637) for limited partnership structures, as applicable to a Foreign-Invested Partnership electing limited liability status
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry (Companies Ordinance Section 67) and the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department (Business Registration Ordinance, Cap. 310)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Form NNC1 (Incorporation Form for Company Limited by Shares) or Form LP1/LPF1 for limited partnership registration; Business Registration Application Form IRBR1
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement for Hong Kong limited partnerships or foreign-invested partnership vehicles; no blocked escrow account requirement. The partnership agreement freely determines capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, and withdrawal mechanics, subject only to anti-money laundering and sanctions compliance under the Hong Kong Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION IN WRITING OF THE INITIAL GOVERNING BOARD OF THE FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP (FIP), CN_FIP, REGISTERED IN HONG KONG SAR, ADOPTED PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 12 OF THE PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT AND THE LAWS OF HONG KONG.

1. SHARE CAPITAL AND CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION: RESOLVED THAT the initial capital commitments of the Partners, as set forth in Schedule A of the Partnership Agreement, be and are hereby approved, and that the General Partner be and is hereby authorized to subscribe for, accept, and receive the aggregate initial capital contribution of HK$1.00 and any additional contributions as may be required for regulatory filings, and to open and maintain a blocked escrow account, if legally mandated, for the sole purpose of fulfilling capital verification requirements in the People's Republic of China, provided that no such escrow is required under Hong Kong law.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED THAT the Partnership's primary bank account(s) be established with a licensed bank in Hong Kong and, where operationally necessary, with a licensed bank in the People's Republic of China through the relevant branch for RMB settlement; RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the General Partner, the Compliance Officer, and the Chief Financial Officer are hereby jointly and severally authorized to open, operate, sign, endorse, and withdraw funds from the said accounts, subject to the two-signature rule for all transfers exceeding HK$50,000 or USD 6,500 equivalent, and subject to the Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Know-Your-Customer (KYC) clearance procedures of the financial institution.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED THAT the registered office of the Partnership be and is hereby established at the address designated in the Application for Business Registration and the Partnership Registration Statement, being a physical address within the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and that the Registered Agent is authorized to file the applicable change-of-address notice with the Companies Registry and the Business Registration Office upon any relocation.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED THAT the following statutory officers be and are hereby appointed: (a) the General Partner as the Managing Partner with full power to bind the Partnership; (b) the Secretary, being an individual ordinarily resident in Hong Kong, to maintain the statutory registers, minute books, and filing docket; (c) the Compliance Officer for the purposes of AML/CFT supervision under Cap. 615; and (d) the Tax Representative for the purpose of receiving notices from the Inland Revenue Department. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT each officer is authorized to execute, attest, and verify all statutory declarations, instruments, and certificates necessary to effectuate these resolutions.

5. GENERAL POWERS: RESOLVED THAT the Partnership shall adopt a common seal, if required, and that any two officers jointly may affix such seal only upon production of a written resolution of the General Partner. RESOLVED THAT this resolution is effective immediately and shall be filed in the statutory minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Reservation through the Companies Registry Integrated Filing System
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry, Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an exhaustive name search against the Register of Companies to confirm that the proposed English and/or Chinese name of the Foreign-Invested Partnership does not conflict with existing registered names, trademarks, or protected statutory names. Submit an electronic Name Reservation Application via ICRIS or the e-Registry portal, specifying the intended entity type (limited partnership or foreign-invested partnership). The proposed name must not contain words that are offensive, imply a connection to the Hong Kong government, or create a false trading association with an existing entity. Reserve the name for an initial period not exceeding three months. Attain a Certificate of Name Reservation, which will be a mandatory prerequisite for the subsequent registration filing.
required_dossiers: Completed Name Reservation Application NNC1-schedule or online equivalent
Identity certificate of the authorized applicant (passport copy or Hong Kong Identity Card)
Proposed partnership name in English and non-mandatory Chinese translation
Supporting search report from ICRIS confirming no identical or misleadingly similar name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or placed on a cautionary list, file a written objection within 14 days, submit an alternative name list of up to three options, and appear before the Registry's Name Review Committee if required; the Registry will re-process within 3 business days upon receipt of the curative submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Partnership Registration and Foreign-Invested Partnership File Submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry (for Limited Partnership Fund or partnership registration) and jointly with the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Partnership Agreement, which must contain the partnership name, nature of business (namely programmatic advertising technology, DSP/SSP real-time ad exchange, and associated data analytics), capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios, management rights, dispute resolution mechanism, and indemnity clauses. File the completed registration form (LP1 for limited partnership or LPF1 for Limited Partnership Fund) together with the partnership agreement and the Incorporation Form NNC1 (if a company is the general partner) to the Companies Registry. Simultaneously submit Form IRBR1 to the Business Registration Office for issuance of the Business Registration Certificate. If the partnership has any non-Hong Kong partners, attach authenticated copies of their constitutional documents and passports. Ensure the stated business address is a physical Hong Kong address and the designated representative is a Hong Kong resident individual or a licensed trust or company service provider.
required_dossiers: Form LPF1/LP1 (signed by all general partners)
Form NNC1 if a corporate general partner is being incorporated simultaneously
Partnership Agreement (original or certified true copy)
Certified passport copies and proof of residential address of all general partners and individuals with significant control
Certificate of Name Reservation (issued in Step 1)
Consent to Act forms for the statutory secretary and compliance officer
Authenticated certificate of incorporation of each corporate partner (for overseas entities)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a notice of query, the partnership has 14 days to respond via an amended filing accompanied by a cover letter explaining the correction; if the application is suspended due to incomplete partner KYC, the designated filing agent must resubmit with supplementary due diligence records and the Registry will recommence processing within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Inland Revenue Department Profile Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department (11/F, Revenue Tower, Wan Chai, Hong Kong)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Certificate of Registration from the Companies Registry, apply to the Business Registration Office under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310). Complete Form IRBR1, declaring the business name, nature of business (ISIC 7310 - Advertising; NAICS 541810 - Advertising Agencies), address of principal place of business in Hong Kong, date of commencement, and estimated monthly revenue for the purpose of determining the appropriate business registration fee and levy. Pay the corresponding statutory fee (currently HKD 2,150 per year plus a HK$150 levy for the protection of wages on insolvency, subject to legislative adjustment), and receive the Business Registration Certificate and Certificate of Registration. This certificate must be displayed at the registered office and renew before the expiry date each year. Register the partnership for Profits Tax through the same file number, ensuring the classification as a pass-through entity for Hong Kong tax purposes, and elect for exclusion from local tax if the partnership's income is wholly derived outside Hong Kong, subject to written confirmation from the Inland Revenue Department.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration from Companies Registry
Form IRBR1 completed and signed
Partnership Agreement summary sheet
Lease agreement or ownership deed for the Hong Kong registered address
Identity copy of the tax representative and general partner
AMR (Annual Return) filing schedule for subsequent years
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Office assesses a higher fee category or requests further financial projections, submit an amended income declaration with a certified statement from the external auditor; if the certificate is delayed, obtain a temporary certificate in writing within 1 business day by presenting the Registry receipt and paying an expedited fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Chinese Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) Filing with MOFCOM and SAMR
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and local Market Supervision Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Given the entity identifier 'CN_FIP', the Hong Kong-incorporated partnership must file for formal recognition as a Foreign-Invested Partnership in the People's Republic of China under the Foreign Investment Law and Implementation Rules. Submit the Foreign Investment Information Report through the Integrated Foreign Investment Platform, including the partnership's constitutional documents, certificate of incorporation from Hong Kong, apostilled and notarized copies, the identification documents of all foreign partners, and a declaration of the actual controlling parties. Apply for the FIP business license at the local Market Supervision Administration, selecting the industry classification '7310' for advertising and the commercial model description for programmatic advertising DSP/SSP. The FIP license will state the registered capital contribution schedule, which may be zero-denominated if permitted, and the business scope must explicitly include 'programmatic advertising technology platform operations; real-time ad exchange; data processing services; digital marketing and SSP services.' Complete the enterprise information archival filing, obtain the statistical registration code, and open an RMB basic deposit account at a branch of a licensed Chinese bank, submitting the Foreign Exchange Registration Form to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for any inbound capital contribution.
required_dossiers: Hong Kong Certificate of Registration and Business Registration Certificate (apostilled)
Partnership Agreement and all amendments (notarized and Chinese translated)
Foreign Investment Information Report form
Passport copies of all foreign partners with notarial certification and visa status
Resume and identity of the proposed legal representative or managing partner
Lease agreement of the intended China operational office
Certificate of approval from the local Commerce Department, if the business scope includes value-added telecommunication services
Safe foreign exchange registration form for capital account transactions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOFCOM or SAMR issues a rectification notice, cure the identified deficiencies within 30 days by submitting supplementary notarized or apostilled documentation; if the application is formally denied on grounds of negative list restrictions, restructure the business scope to exclude prohibited activities or transfer the relevant activities to a separate wholly foreign-owned enterprise; if the license is withheld due to incomplete SAFE registration, engage a certified accountant to submit the audit trail of capital contribution within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity operates exclusively as a digital programmatic advertising exchange and supply-side platform conducting no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating permit required; only general business registration and, if applicable, a Value-Added Telecommunication Services (VATS) license for certain data exchange services under the Telecommunications Ordinance of China, subject to separate legal review.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no physical project is being constructed or operated; the environmental permitting regime of the Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) of China applies to physical facilities only, and this entity performs no discharge, emission, or hazardous waste-generating activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Full EIA Report, Environmental Registration, and Pollution Discharge Permit are all Not Applicable because the entity is a pure digital services operation (ISIC 7310) with no physical plant.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, zero hazardous waste generation; the entity's only infrastructure is cloud-hosted servers and data centers, which are subject to their operator's environmental compliance, not the FIP's direct permitting obligation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no physical premises subject to Hong Kong Civil Defense fire safety certification or China Fire Department (消防) approval for storage/assembly; the only occupation is office-based software engineering and ad operations for which standard commercial office fire safety compliance is covered by the leasing or office property's existing certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Hong Kong SAR Government; electronic portal: GovHK eTAX (https://www.etax.gov.hk); Business Registration Office of the IRD for Business Registration Certificates.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File for registration as a limited partnership with the Companies Registry under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) or Limited Partnership Fund Ordinance (Cap. 637) if an LPF structure is chosen; this is a legal prerequisite for the entity's existence and must be completed before tax registration. Step 2: Within one month of commencement of business, apply for Business Registration (BR) under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) using official Form IRBR1 (Application for Business Registration) submitted to the Business Registration Office of the IRD. The application must include the partnership's registered name, address, and description of business. For a foreign non-resident partner, attach a certified copy of its overseas registration certificate, and provide a Hong Kong correspondence address for IRD notice purposes. Step 3: The IRD will issue the Business Registration Certificate (BRC) bearing an 8-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which functions as the partnership's de facto tax identification number. The BRN must be displayed at the business premises and used on invoices and correspondence. Step 4: The IRD will allocate an Inland Revenue file number to the partnership and issue Profits Tax Returns (Partnership) on a basis period. A 'Principal Partner' (or the partnership's authorized representative) is responsible for completing and filing the return. Step 5: Each partner (individual or corporate) must separately provide tax identification details: Hong Kong individuals use their HKID card numbers; foreign non-resident individuals must provide their passport number and a current foreign tax identification number; foreign corporate partners must provide proof of incorporation and their overseas tax registration number. The IRD uses this information to assess each partner on their share of partnership profits. No separate VAT/GST registration is required because Hong Kong has no such tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Hong Kong does not operate a 'check-the-box' election regime. Partnerships are statutorily transparent for income tax purposes under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112); profits and losses are allocated to partners and assessed in their hands. There are no hybrid mismatch elections available for this entity type in Hong Kong.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Not Applicable – Hong Kong does not impose VAT, GST, or general sales and use tax. The territory relies on direct taxes (profits tax, salaries tax, property tax) and selective duties (e.g., liquor, tobacco) which are outside the scope of this entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable. There is no turnover-based registration threshold for indirect tax because no indirect tax is levied. However, every business, including a service partnership, must register for Business Registration under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Hong Kong does not require electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API-based submission of invoices, or anti-fraud digital stamping. Commercial invoices and receipts are issued under common law practice and retained for at least 7 years under the Inland Revenue Ordinance. Electronic invoicing is permitted but not mandated by statute.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. As Hong Kong has no VAT/GST, there is no export zero-rating regime. Cross-border services, including programmatic advertising provided from Hong Kong, are outside the scope of indirect tax. For profits tax purposes, income is chargeable only if sourced in Hong Kong under the territorial source principle; services wholly performed outside Hong Kong may be reported as non-taxable offshore income, supported by contracts, evidence of negotiation and execution abroad, and client communications.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable for services; no customs or foreign exchange repatriation documentation is required for intangible service exports from Hong Kong. For physical goods exported from Hong Kong, the statutory bundle would include: Electronic Export Declaration (under the Import and Export (Registration) Regulations, Cap. 60), a Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, a Commercial Invoice, and a Packing List. Inward Remittance Certificates are not issued in Hong Kong because there are no exchange controls.

For substantiating offshore profits treatment (not indirect tax), IRD practice expects the following evidence: executed or scanned contracts signed outside Hong Kong, board meeting minutes or management decision records showing off-HK oversight, correspondence with non-HK customers, bank statements showing receipts from foreign markets, and project specifications showing performance of services outside the territory.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: As there is no indirect tax, no clawback of VAT zero-rating can arise. However, if a taxpayer claims profits-tax exemption for offshore income without adequate supporting evidence, the Inland Revenue Department may disregard the claim, raise additional assessments under section 60 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (additional tax up to 100% of the undercharged tax if no fraud, and 200% in cases of fraud), and impose penalties under section 82A. Criminal prosecution leading to fines and imprisonment is also possible where wilful evasion is established. The IRD can audit records up to 6 years (10 years where fraud was involved).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) in its capacity as the de facto central bank and Exchange Fund administrator for the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; for cross-boundary RMB flows to and from mainland China, the People's Bank of China and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) also have regulatory authority over the onshore side.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Hong Kong operates a fully convertible open capital account under the Linked Exchange Rate System. The Hong Kong dollar is freely convertible outside mainland China and there is no legal distinction between current account and capital account convertibility for ordinary treasury operations. Non-residents and foreign-invested partnerships may maintain offshore RMB (CNH), HKD, USD, EUR or JPY accounts without HKMA approval, fund them from abroad, and remit profits, dividends, or repayment of shareholder loans without surrender or mandatory conversion requirements. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in their original or any permitted currency, and no foreign exchange control or central bank filing is required before remitting for trade or financial purposes. The only meaningful friction lies at the PRC border: capital injections from mainland China must comply with the regulatory framework for outward direct investment, including NDRC filing and SAFE registration, and each remittance must satisfy genuine-transaction review by the Chinese remitting bank. Once the funds are received in Hong Kong, they can be freely diverted to operational expenses, publisher payments, tax, or shareholder distributions, and the HKD/USD exchange rate is stable because the HKMA maintains a tight convertibility band at 7.75 to 7.85. Therefore, treasury planning should prioritise pre-clearance of source-side PRC remittances rather than Hong Kong restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender rules in Hong Kong. The HKMA does not impose any timeline for repatriation, forced conversion, or ratio requirement for foreign exchange receipts. An exporter may keep the full invoice amount in an operational HKD, USD, or CNH account, convert it at market rates, or use it to pay trade obligations without needing any central bank declaration. If the FIP settles advertising invoices from Chinese clients, the CNH proceeds can be held offshore and are not subject to mainland China surrender or settlement rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (HSBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow account and multi-currency operational HKD/USD current account
Capital escrow account plus dedicated offshore RMB account for cross-boundary service collections
Basic operational multi-currency account and trade finance / treasury limits
Operational current account for payroll and publisher disbursement operations

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-medium as a primary account, medium as an ancillary collection rail. The Hong Kong Banking Ordinance restricts deposit-taking to licensed authorised institutions; pure offshore EMI licences do not permit deposit-taking in Hong Kong and are not regulated by the HKMA, so they cannot serve as the bank-of-record for a foreign-invested partnership. HK-licensed virtual banks, such as Mox Bank, WeLab Bank and Livi Bank, are authorised institutions and can open basic HKD/USD accounts, but their trade finance, FX hedging, CHATS clearing, and credit capabilities are limited and they generally impose lower transaction thresholds than tier-1 incumbents. An offshore EMI with only an EU/UK e-money licence is vulnerable to inbound remittance rejection by HK compliance, particularly when the ultimate beneficial owner sits in mainland China. Consequently, the partnership should maintain its primary treasury and capital-escrow relationship at a tier-1 commercial bank, and may use a regulated money service operator or virtual bank only for small-ticket disbursements with full reporting to the principal bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: General partners and all authorised signatories are normally required to appear in person at the Hong Kong branch for initial account opening, although HKMA-codified remote video KYC has become accepted at tier-1 banks for low-risk Hong Kong residents. For an FIP whose general partner or ultimate beneficial owner is a mainland China corporate or individual, banks almost always require one of the following: in-branch interview in Hong Kong; a notarised copy of passport and power-of-attorney attested by a Hong Kong solicitor or certified public accountant; or a remote interview coupled with a professional introducer referral from an existing HSBC, BOCHK, or Standard Chartered client. Proxy opening by an outside non-professional is generally not permitted. In practice, HSBC and BOCHK permit a structured remote opening only if the partnership provides original KYC documents attested by an accepted HK professional; otherwise physical attendance is mandatory before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red flag 1: multi-tier partnership ownership and politically exposed or opaque controllers creating difficulty in identifying ultimate beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the partnership agreement and all amendments; full legal entity ownership chart with each partner at or above 10% and every general partner regardless of percentage; register of partners with date of joining and capital contribution; passports, Hong Kong business registration, tax identification numbers, and current residential address proof for all beneficial owners; bank reference or prior account statement from the Chinese parent; signed declaration of source of funds and source of wealth; and a notarised resolution from the general partner appointing authorised signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red flag 2: inbound capital injection from mainland China without verifiable outward direct investment approval, raising concern over illegal capital flight
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE Outward Direct Investment Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate; NDRC overseas investment filing or approval certificate; signed capital contribution or partnership subscription agreement; PRC remitting bank instruction showing the approved ODI purpose code; transaction history from the parent company's onshore bank account clearly identifying the destination as the HK FIP; Hong Kong CPA capital verification certificate; and audited financial statements of the Chinese parent for the last two years with no unexplained diversion of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red flag 3: programmatic ad exchange model exposes the account to third-party incoming funds from many unknown advertisers and outgoing payments to undisclosed global publisher networks, resembling money laundering or commingling
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: HKMA-compliant AML and counter-terrorist financing manual; transactional monitoring system configuration note; platform-level customer onboarding policy and negative news screening output; current list of approved advertisers, ad buyers, procurement agencies, and publisher settlement accounts; executed master services agreements with publishers and DSP/SSP clients; monthly contract settlement statements showing gross billing and commission deductions aligned to bank entries; and a third-party independent AML gap assessment or legal opinion confirming that the platform does not allow anonymous bidding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red flag 4: potential sanctions exposure because global ad-serving and SSP traffic may originate from countries subject to OFAC, EU, or UN embargoes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening log covering all counterparties and final beneficial owners; IP-based geo-blocking and prohibited-country policy with screenshots from the platform's technical control; contract clauses obligating access from non-sanctioned territories and the FIP's public compliance statement; passport, residence, and business records for every customer with an annual spend above HKD 100,000; end-to-end transaction trail for a sample of payments from the highest-risk region; and a legal opinion from a Hong Kong law firm confirming sanctions compliance and absence of designated-party relationships.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The PRC parent should have completed NDRC project filing and SAFE ODI registration for its investment in the Hong Kong FIP before opening the HK bank account or remitting funds. At execution, the onshore bank remits via SWIFT MT103 with a narrative referencing partnership capital contribution, the SAFE ODI certificate number, and the purpose code for outbound direct investment equity or quasi-equity capital. The HK receiving bank will not require Hong Kong Monetary Authority approval, but will ask to see the remitter's identity, the underlying partnership agreement, and a board or general partner resolution approving the contribution. For capital verification, a Hong Kong certified public accountant can issue a certificate after receipt of funds; this certificate is useful for the PRC parent's annual ODI monitoring, Hong Kong profits tax filing, and future dividend or return-of-capital remittances. No minimum capital is statutorily required for the Hong Kong FIP, but most tier-1 banks expect initial operating deposits of at least HKD 500,000 or equivalent to justify account economics and support the capital-escrow classification. The funds may remain in HKD, USD or CNH and can be freely converted into other convertible currencies once inside Hong Kong.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound disbursements to publishers, data partners and technology vendors, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for individual cross-border transfers above HKD 100,000. For Hong Kong domestic payments in HKD, the clearing rail is CHATS; USD and CNH payments also have dedicated CHATS clearing systems that are faster and more cost-effective than legacy correspondent wires. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are only relevant if the FIP is financing physical trade or importing hardware for ad-serving or hardware-based exchanges; in that case a standard confirmed irrevocable L/C may be issued through HSBC or Standard Chartered. In every disbursement, the beneficiary name, bank account, and invoice reference must be explicitly stated on the wire narrative; payments to a pooled wallet belonging to an intermediary or affiliate should be avoided unless supported by a written treasury instruction and a reconciliation report. ACH-style direct settlement is acceptable for payroll and low-value publisher micropayments, but the partner's core trade settlement ledger should retain MT103 or CHATS confirmations so that the documentary evidence is sufficient for internal audit, customs, and tax inspections.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards between HKD, USD, EUR, JPY and CNH to hedge committed advertising service revenue and publisher obligations
Offshore RMB (CNH) non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for addressing exposure to onshore CNY conversion risk, especially where mainland customer receipts are pending conversion
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) to restructure HKD, USD, and CNH financing and swap fixed or floating interest rate exposures for long-term capital
Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars with approved HKMA-licensed or international-domiciled counterparties under a standard ISDA credit support annex

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate Renewal under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after each anniversary of the Business Registration Certificate effective date; the renewal demand is normally despatched one month before expiry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs an overdue fine of HK$300 (about USD 38); persistent default may lead to prosecution, a maximum fine of HK$5,000 (about USD 641), and administrative strike-off of the business from the Business Register, which immediately terminates legal trading capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for Partnership (Form BIR52) and tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department - Profits Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one month of the issue date; for standard 31 March year-end returns filed through a licensed tax representative, the mandatory extension deadline is 15 August of the following year of assessment, further extendable to 15 November for non-standard year ends.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), late filing first triggers a penalty of HK$1,200 (about USD 154); where a best-of-judgment assessment is raised, the penalty increases to HK$3,000 (about USD 385) plus a 5% default surcharge on tax, and on court conviction the fine may reach HK$10,000 (about USD 1,282) plus three times the tax undercharged.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (BIR56A and BIR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department - Employer's Returns Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 30 April immediately after the year of assessment ends on 31 March; a NIL return is mandatory if no employees were engaged.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing renders the employer liable to a fine of HK$10,000 (about USD 1,282) and an additional tax default penalty of up to three times the amount; willful neglect may also expose the general partner to revenue seizure and prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited Partnership Annual Return / Annual Particulars Confirmation under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 321)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: To be delivered during January of each year, or within 28 days of the anniversary of registration if using an anniversary-based electronic filing regime; a nil confirmation is accepted when no particulars have changed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default continues at HK$50 (about USD 6.4) per day up to a maximum of HK$50,000 (about USD 6,410); the Companies Registry may administratively strike the limited partnership off the register, causing the loss of limited liability shield for limited partners.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Hong Kong law, a partnership vehicle is not automatically audited; however, where the entity elects corporate form, the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s.141D requires independent CPA audit for any company exceeding any two of these three thresholds in a financial year: annual revenue over HKD 20,000,000 (about USD 2.56 million), total assets over HKD 20,000,000 (about USD 2.56 million), or headcount over 50 employees. A Hong Kong limited partnership fund (LPF) under Cap. 637, even if a partnership, must always appoint a certified public accountant and present audited financial statements to the Inland Revenue Department with its profits tax return.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) and HKFRS for Private Entities (HKFRS-PE), issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA), supported by the Professional Accountants Ordinance and HKICPA auditing standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not require a public UBO register for partnerships; nevertheless the general partner must complete an annual internal verification on or before 15 January, confirming every partner's identity, contribution, profit share and any change in control. Any transfer or variation of partnership interests, capital accounts or profit-sharing ratios must be documented in writing and, if registration particulars are affected, be reported to the Inland Revenue Department Business Registration Office and to the Companies Registry within 30 days of the event. Where a licensed trust or company service provider is engaged, the anti-money-laundering verification under Cap. 615 must also be refreshed annually.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (or Register of Partners), Register of Directors (or Register of General Partners), Register of Charges/Mortgages, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - 600 per annum for registered office and corporate secretarial agent services in Hong Kong
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 6,000 per annum for a certified CPA audit of a small-to-medium AdTech partnership under HKFRS

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% on assessable profits exceeding HK$2 million, with a reduced rate of 7.5% on the first HK$2 million for unincorporated partnerships; if the Foreign-Invested Partnership is retrofitted as a corporation, the headline rate is 16.5% (8.25% on first HK$2 million)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Two-tiered profits tax; patent box incentive at 5% for qualifying intellectual property profits; 200% tax deduction for first HK$2 million qualifying R&D expenditure and 150% for the excess; offshore profits exemption for profits sourced outside Hong Kong; 0% profits tax on qualified carried interest distributed by eligible limited partnership funds; exemption for qualifying fund transactions under sections 20AC and 20AN of the Inland Revenue Ordinance
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (unlimited carry-forward of assessed partnership losses under Inland Revenue Ordinance section 70)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profits Tax Return – Form BIR52 for Hong Kong partnerships (including Foreign-Invested Partnerships); filed through the IRD eTAX electronic filing system (https://www.eTAX.gov.hk). The precedent partner or authorised tax representative of the FIP must file the partnership return, and non-resident partners are separately assessed and may receive Form BIR55 / Profits Tax Return for Non-Resident Persons.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 1 month from the date the return is issued by the Inland Revenue Department. For accounting periods ending between 1 April and 30 November, an automatic paper filing extension is generally granted to 3 May of the following year and eTAX filing to 3 May; for periods ending in December or January, extensions through 15 June or 30 June are available on application by the tax representative. Failure to file by the extended deadline renders the entire deemed assessment final under IRO section 59.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales, commission, fees and other operating receipts from programmatic advertising, DSP/SSP exchange activities, and ad-tech services before deductions and rebates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full gross ad-exchange turnover attributable to contracts negotiated, booking, and traffic auctions conducted through Hong Kong servers. If the non-resident partner intends to claim offshore character for income booked in China or elsewhere, an itemised territorial source statement must be annexed showing where contracts were concluded, where supply chain decisions were made, and where the servers are operated. IRD will disregard unsupported claims and re-source income to Hong Kong under the conservative test for value creation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income and all other non-operating income, including bank deposit interest, shared ad-tech infrastructure rental income, and income from treasury activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest derived from Hong Kong bank accounts is Hong Kong-sourced and chargeable. Interest paid by a non-Hong Kong borrower to the FIP may be excluded if the contractual negotiations, loan execution, and beneficial enjoyment occur entirely outside Hong Kong. Non-resident partners must ensure that the profits tax return does not rely on the now-stricken default exemption for intra-group interest under section 15(1)(i), and must attach a computation of Hong Kong-sourced interest if a cross-border loan is made by the FIP.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Royalty and licence income received by the FIP from intellectual property such as software, algorithms, DSP/SSP data models, and trademark licensing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Gross royalties received by the FIP must be reported even if the payer is a mainland Chinese affiliate. If the IP is used in or outside Hong Kong, determine assessability under section 15(1)(a) and (b). The Hong Kong recipient may be entitled to a foreign tax credit if the mainland payer withheld under the China-Hong Kong Arrangement, provided a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership statement are included with the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income: sum of Box 1, Box 2, Box 3 and any other income, adjusted to the accounting profit before deductible expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the aggregation point for the partnership's assessable income. For non-resident partners, special attention is needed to avoid double-counting of profits already taxed in China via a permanent establishment. The FIP must not net expenses before arriving at Box 4; expenses and deductions are entered separately. If any non-resident partner is a mainland resident individual or corporation, the Box 4 total may be scrutinised for re-allocation under section 61A if the partnership is used as a foreign investment vehicle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: commission paid to publishers, cloud-hosting fees, data-centre charges, personnel costs, legal and professional fees, and other expenses wholly and exclusively incurred in producing assessable profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses that meet the Inland Revenue Ordinance section 16 test. For intercompany payments made to a connected Chinese or offshore DSP/SSP entity, the expense is deductible only to the extent of the arm's length amount under sections 16(1)(b) and 20AB. Non-resident partners should be aware that any deductible expense paid to a related party must be supported by transfer pricing documentation showing CUP/margin comparables; otherwise the IRD will disallow the expense and adjust the partnership profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted assessable profit or loss before distribution to partners, after adding back disallowable expenses and applying statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The FIP as a pass-through entity reports this figure; do not pay profits tax at the entity level. For each non-resident partner, the partnership allocation is computed on a fair market basis. The IRD may reassess a non-resident partner's share on a source and accrual basis even if the partner is not ordinarily resident in Hong Kong. If this Box shows a loss, confirm that the non-resident partner has no separate Hong Kong business loss ring-fencing restrictions; partnership loss carry-forward is allowed only against the same partner's partnership profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner allocation schedule: each partner's name, tax registration number, profit-sharing ratio, allocated taxable profit, and the partner's two-tiered rate election.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident partner, complete the schedule with the partner's overseas address and Chinese tax resident ID where applicable. Each partner elects for the 7.5%/15% two-tiered rate on their distributed share; however, the reduced concession is denied if the partner is also claiming the HK$2 million band through another unincorporated business. For mainland-resident partners, attach a copy of the Tax Residency Certificate and a statement that no double counting of the same loss is being used in mainland China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: DTA housekeeping and offshore claim declaration: box on the supplementary statement where the partnership declares whether any DTA relief, external tax credit, or offshore exemption is claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Hong Kong does not impose a withholding tax on distributions to partners, so no DTA relief is required at the FIP level for outbound profit sharing. However, if the FIP claims that part of the ad-tech income is offshore because the servers and sales force are in mainland China, the non-resident partners must document core income-generating activities located outside Hong Kong. This Box must be consistent with the transfer pricing Master File; omitted information will trigger an investigation and potential 3-year fraud uplift of the assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: IRO section 80(1) maximum fine of HK$10,000; continued default after conviction adds HK$100 per day for each day the return remains delinquent. If the return is filed more than 6 months late without reasonable excuse, the IRD may demand an estimated assessment under section 59; penalties are doubled for intentional evasion. For fraudulent or negligent submission of false information, IRO sections 82 and 82A impose a maximum fine of HK$50,000, treble the tax undercharged, and imprisonment for up to 3 years. eTAX electronic filing failure after a court direction may additionally result in a fine of HK$100,000. For partnerships in particular, the precedent partner is personally liable for penalties; the IRD may collect the penalty from any partner of the FIP if the precedent partner is outside Hong Kong.
